plan.melodySummary: The iconic theme migrates through dark solo voices—beginning with the plaintive Oboe, sinking into the shadowy English Horn, brightening only briefly at the climax before the Tenor Sax and Cello draw it back down into darkness. Dynamics hover between !pp! and !mp!, swelling only once near mm.13-16 before dissolving into an unresolved hush.

sections.label: Phrase A — First Light in Shadow
sections.notes: Play the theme alone and exposed at !pp!, thin and searching; let the isolated entrance ring over silence. Cello enters only under Am/E7 downbeats with a sustained low open fifth, softer than the Oboe.

sections.label: Phrase A' — Deeper Descent
sections.notes: Take over the theme in its dark low register at !pp!, mournful and veiled; leave phrase-ends hanging unresolved. Cello sustains bare fifths beneath, never louder than the melody.

sections.label: Phrase B — The Climb
sections.notes: The single swell of the piece: begin !mp! and rise toward the high point at mm.15-16, brighter and more open. English Horn shadows a half-step below at !p! as a chromatic neighbor haze; Cello tremolo shimmer at !pp! only, always under the melody.

sections.label: Phrase A'' — Dissolve
sections.notes: Draw the theme back to darkness at !pp!, breathy and hollow in the low register; let the final A fade unresolved into silence. Cello holds one sustained low fifth beneath, quieter than the Sax.

Oboe.instruction: The primary voice of light in shadow. Play at !pp!–!mp!, thin and plaintive; only swell during mm.13-16. Leave phrase endings breathing and unresolved, never rushing the silences.

English Horn.instruction: Carry the theme in mm.9-12 in your darkest low register at !pp!. Elsewhere (mm.13-18) act as a chromatic neighbor-tone shadow at !p!, always softer than the Oboe. Tacet in outer phrases.

Tenor Sax.instruction: Silent until mm.19, then take the theme low, breathy and hollow at !pp!, drawing the piece into darkness. Let the closing A dissolve unresolved.

Cello.instruction: The lone foundation throughout: sustained low open fifths and half-diminished colors under harmonic changes only, entering where it truly matters. Stay !pp! and always beneath the current melody carrier; use faint tremolo shimmer during mm.13-16 for the single swell, then settle to one held fifth at the close.
